vulnerability_analysis: The CoinToken contract has owner-only functions that control tax wallets and tax rates. The owner can set tax wallets to any address and set arbitrary tax percentages. By setting tax wallets to attacker-controlled addresses and setting high tax rates, the attacker can siphon ETH from trades. The handleTax() function collects taxes during trades and distributes ETH to the tax wallets. Since the owner controls these wallets, they can redirect all tax revenue to themselves.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank. 2. Set tax wallets (dev, marketing, charity) to attacker-controlled addresses. 3. Set high buy and sell tax rates to maximize tax collection. 4. Execute a buy transaction to trigger buy tax accumulation. 5. Execute a sell transaction to trigger sell tax processing and ETH distribution. 6. Collect ETH from the attacker-controlled tax wallets.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.startPrank(owner) to impersonate owner. 2. Call setTaxWallets() with attacker addresses. 3. Call setBuyTax() and setSellTax() with high values (e.g., 25 each). 4. Prepare for trade: get WETH, approve token spending. 5. Buy tokens via Uniswap pair to trigger buy tax. 6. Sell tokens back via Uniswap pair to trigger sell tax processing. 7. Collect ETH balances from tax wallet addresses.
